payload.task_text:
You are a researcher on an ML team. Your principal investigator has asked you to catalog the curated ML technology videos from a channel called ML Tech Reviews on the video platform. This channel has a dedicated playlist of 7 videos, each covering a specific open-source machine learning project with a corresponding code repository. You need to catalog these videos, cross-reference them with related research papers from your local paper library, build a knowledge base page for the team, compile an Excel research tracker, and send a summary email.

Your workflow should proceed as follows.

First, retrieve the ML Tech Reviews playlist from the video platform. Get all items in the playlist. For each of the 7 videos, fetch the full details including the title, description, tags, publication date, and view count. From each video description, extract any repository link that points to a code hosting service. Identify the primary ML topic or technique that the video covers, such as Flash Attention, LoRA, Diffusion Models, RLHF, Mixture of Experts, Quantization, or Vector Databases, based on the title and tags.

Second, search your local paper library for research papers related to each of the 7 ML topics you identified. For each topic, retrieve the paper details including the paper identifier, title, authors, and publication date.

Third, create an Excel file named ML_Research_Tracker.xlsx. Create a sheet named Videos with these columns in order: Video_ID, Title, Topic, GitHub_URL, Published_Date, View_Count. Populate it with one row for each of the 7 videos. Create a second sheet named Papers with these columns: ArXiv_ID, Title, Authors, Published, Topic, Related_Video_ID. Populate it with one row per paper found, linking each paper to its related video by the video identifier. Create a third sheet named Summary with these columns: Topic, Video_Count, Paper_Count, GitHub_Repos_Count. Populate it with one row per topic, summarizing the counts.

Write every date (Published_Date and Published) as a plain YYYY-MM-DD value, and write every count and number as a literal value — do not use spreadsheet formulas. If the work is split across sub-agents, aggregate all results into this single ML_Research_Tracker.xlsx file so it is complete (all 7 videos and every paper found) before you finish.

Fourth, create a new page in the team knowledge base titled "ML Tech Research Hub". Add an introductory paragraph describing the purpose of the page and the channel being cataloged. Then create a database within the knowledge base titled "Research Items" with the following properties: Name as the title field, Type as a select field with options Video and Paper, Topic as a text field, URL as a text field, and Status as a select field with options New, In Review, and Archived. Add an entry for each of the 7 videos and for each paper you found.

Fifth, send an email to research@lab.edu. The subject should reference the ML research catalog. The body should summarize the number of videos cataloged, the number of papers found, the topics covered, and mention that the full details are in ML_Research_Tracker.xlsx and in the team knowledge base.

The research configuration file in your workspace is named research_config.md and explains the cataloging approach. A topic mapping file named topic_mapping.json lists the 7 expected ML topics to use as reference.

When all outputs are complete, claim the task as done.

Task-Solving Rationable with Sub-task Decomposition:
To solve this task efficiently, complete it directly in the main agent and dispatch no sub-agent. The source is one bounded seven-video playlist plus a local paper library; the direct route avoids topic/writer handoffs and prevents paper metadata from being guessed between agents.

Dynamically resolve and read `research_config.md` plus `topic_mapping.json`. Retrieve the dedicated `ML Tech Reviews` playlist once, then call `playlists_getPlaylistItems(playlistId=<retained playlist ID>, maxResults=50)` exactly once; this handler has no cursor argument. Require seven unique observed video IDs, fetch full details for each, and preserve returned IDs, titles, descriptions, tags, publication dates, integer views, and every repository URL in a description. Map each video to exactly one of the seven literal topic labels using its title, tags, and description.

Search the local paper library for every one of the seven runtime topic labels. Build seven bounded queries before issuing them in one native-parallel response. When a video's description exposes an arXiv ID or distinctive paper title, use that reference as the narrow query and require the returned ID/title to match it; otherwise use the literal mapped topic plus the video's strongest title/tag terms. Each call uses `max_results=5` and `sort_by="relevance"`, with only the topic-appropriate categories from the visible mapping/config when supplied. Retain every unique returned paper that is directly relevant to that topic, and retain none merely because it shares a generic ML term. Preserve only tool-returned `id`, exact title, complete returned author list, `published` normalized to `YYYY-MM-DD`, and URL; never synthesize or overwrite a date. A topic may legitimately have no directly relevant local result, but that conclusion must come from its executed search rather than being predeclared. Freeze one canonical payload with exactly seven Videos rows, one Papers row per verified result, and seven Summary rows derived from those runtime results.

The main agent is the sole writer of `ML_Research_Tracker.xlsx` and the `ML Tech Research Hub`/`Research Items` Notion structure. Create the workbook once with exact `Videos`, `Papers`, and `Summary` headers; use literal values and no formulas, then read all three sheets back and compare all seven video IDs, every verified paper ID/date/author row, topic joins, repository URLs, and derived counts to the payload. For Notion, search exact titles first; create or complete one nonduplicate page/database with the required property types and topic options, then upsert one item per canonical video and paper using stable video/paper IDs and retrieve the schema and all runtime rows. Do not retry an ambiguous create. Finally reconcile workbook and Notion IDs/counts, check Sent mail, send only one missing exact-recipient/subject summary with verified counts and deliverable references, read back the sent record, and call `claim_done`.

Create a knowledge base structure in Notion using the Notion API tools.

STEP 1 — Create the hub page:
Create a top-level Notion page titled "ML Tech Research Hub" (parent: none / workspace root — do NOT create it inside an existing database; if you need a parent, use API-post-search to find an appropriate top-level location or create it as a standalone page). Add to the page body an introductory paragraph with content similar to:
"This page catalogs curated ML technology videos from the ML Tech Reviews channel on the video platform, together with related research papers from our local paper library. The channel deep-dives into open-source machine learning projects — covering topics such as Flash Attention, LoRA, Diffusion Models, RLHF, Mixture of Experts, Quantization, and Vector Databases. Each video is cross-referenced with its code repository and any related papers to give the team a single knowledge base for ML research resources."
(You may refine the wording, but it must describe the page's purpose and the channel being cataloged.)

Within the "ML Tech Research Hub" page, create a database titled "Research Items" with these properties:
- "Name" as the title property
- "Type" as a select property with options: "Video", "Paper"
- "Topic" as a text (rich_text) property
- "URL" as a text (rich_text) property
